documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M, physical. Feels well. Breathing at his usual - albuterol a couple of times a week, more with dust. No flares this past year. Smoking 3/4 to 1 ppd.
ROS: negative for cough change, hemoptysis, weight loss, fevers, chest pain.
Meds: tiotropium daily, albuterol prn. No allergies.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight stable from last year. HEENT normal. Lungs no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular without murmur. Abdomen soft. No clubbing, no edema. No lymphadenopathy.

A/P
- COPD: stable. Continue.
- Pulmonary nodule: followed by pulmonology.
- Tobacco: we talked again about what quitting would do for his lungs. He wants to try on his own this summer.
- Screening: FIT. Labs today.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID in the fall.
RTC fall.

documents.title: Office Visit - cough, weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted Friday asking to come in. Dry cough for about 3 months, not his usual morning cough - comes on through the day, no phlegm. Has lost about 15 lb without trying; belt is two notches tighter. Appetite a bit down. No fever, no night sweats, no blood in what he coughs up. Breathing about baseline otherwise. Still smoking.

O: Weight 77.2 kg, down from 84 at his physical in April. Vitals otherwise as charted, afebrile. Appears well, not in distress. Lungs: breath sounds decreased over the right upper chest; no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. No clubbing.

A/P
Persistent cough and unintentional weight loss in a ~30 pack-year smoker with COPD and a known RLL nodule (pulmonology wanted a repeat CT in 2023). Worried about this. Chest x-ray today; urgent pulmonology referral placed and I called their office directly to get him in this month. Told him honestly why I'm moving fast. He'll text me with anything new.

conditions.label: Lung mass
conditions.note: Right upper lobe mass on chest X-ray, suspected malignancy

reports.text:
PA and lateral views of the chest. Comparison: none.
There is a mass in the right upper lobe. The remainder of the lungs is clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Bones intact.
reports.conclusion: Right upper lobe mass. CT chest recommended.

documents.title: Chest X-ray result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CXR: mass in the right upper lung. Told him this needs a CT and likely a biopsy, and that cancer is the main concern, though we don't know yet. Pulmonology has him 9/27; they'll arrange the CT. His sister is going to drive him. Answered questions. He said he's done with cigarettes - we'll see; offered nicotine patch, he wants to try without.

events.reason: Cough, weight loss, right upper lobe mass

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - OFFICE NOTE
Date of visit: 09/27/2024

Seen in 2022 for a 6 mm right lower lobe nodule. Now referred back urgently by primary care: three months of a new dry cough and an unintended 15 lb weight loss. Denies fevers, night sweats or hemoptysis. Still smoking, cutting down since last week. COPD on tiotropium, albuterol as needed.

Family history: father with COPD; paternal uncle with lung cancer.
Social: construction worker. Current smoker, 30 pack-years. Drinks occasionally.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: afebrile. BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16. Thin, comfortable. Decreased breath sounds over the right upper lobe. No wheeze. No palpable adenopathy.

Data: CBC - Hgb 14 g/dL, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000. Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0, glucose 95.
Chest x-ray 9/17 (reviewed): right upper lobe mass.

Assessment: right upper lobe mass with weight loss in a heavy smoker - suspicious for primary lung cancer.
Plan:
1. CT chest with contrast this week.
2. Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound for tissue and nodal sampling, depending on CT.
3. He understands the concern. Strongly encouraged to stop smoking.

cc: primary care

reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: CT of the chest with intravenous contrast.
COMPARISON: Low-dose CT 09/12/2022; chest radiograph 09/17/2024.
FINDINGS: There is a 4.0 cm mass in the right upper lobe. Mediastinal lymphadenopathy is present. The previously described 6 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe is unchanged. No pleural effusion. No pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No destructive osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right upper lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy, highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. Stable 6 mm right lower lobe nodule.

documents.title: CT chest with contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Report received from the outside imaging center. 4 cm RUL mass with mediastinal adenopathy; RLL 6 mm nodule unchanged since 2022. Routed to PCP; pulmonology also copied.

documents.title: CT reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT. Spoke with pulmonology - bronchoscopy with EBUS booked for 10/9. Called Derek and went over it. He asked whether this is the spot from 2022 - no, that one hasn't changed; this is in the upper lobe.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE REPORT - received 10/10/2024
Date of procedure: 10/09/2024
Procedure: flexible bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration of the right upper lobe mass and mediastinal lymph nodes.
Indication: 4 cm right upper lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation, oral route.
Findings: airways without endobronchial lesion. Enlarged mediastinal nodes visualized by EBUS and sampled; the mass was sampled as well. Rapid on-site evaluation showed malignant cells.
Complications: none. Minimal bleeding.
Disposition: discharged home with his sister. Final pathology to follow.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Non-small cell carcinoma, right upper lobe, mediastinal nodes involved

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: (A) Right upper lobe mass, EBUS-guided FNA. (B) Mediastinal lymph node, EBUS-guided FNA.
MICROSCOPIC: Both specimens contain malignant epithelial cells in cohesive groups, without features of small cell carcinoma. Material is limited for further subtyping.
reports.conclusion: A and B: Non-small cell carcinoma, consistent with primary lung carcinoma.

documents.title: Surgical pathology, EBUS FNA
documents.author: pathology
documents.body: Final pathology received: non-small cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe mass and in the mediastinal lymph node. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Pathology result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology already told him this afternoon. I called after. Non-small cell lung cancer, involving the nodes in the middle of the chest. Staging scans (PET, brain MRI) ordered by pulmonology; oncology referral made by them. He was steady on the phone, sister there with him. Booked to see me after the oncology visit. Problem list updated.

reports.text:
FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh.
The right upper lobe mass is FDG avid. FDG-avid ipsilateral mediastinal lymph nodes. No FDG-avid contralateral mediastinal or supraclavicular nodes. No FDG-avid lesions in the liver, adrenal glands or skeleton. The 6 mm right lower lobe nodule is below PET resolution.
reports.conclusion: FDG-avid right upper lobe mass with ipsilateral mediastinal nodal disease. No distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: PET-CT
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: PET-CT report received. Disease limited to the right upper lobe mass and ipsilateral mediastinal nodes; no distant spread.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. No enhancing lesion. No mass effect, hemorrhage or acute infarct. Ventricles normal in size.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of intracranial metastatic disease.

documents.title: MRI brain
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Brain MRI with and without contrast: normal, no metastases. Received and filed.

events.reason: New diagnosis non-small cell lung cancer

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 10/22/2024

47-year-old construction worker, ~30 pack-year current smoker with COPD, referred by pulmonology for newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer. Presented with 3 months of dry cough and 15 lb weight loss. CT 10/01: 4 cm RUL mass with mediastinal adenopathy. EBUS-FNA 10/09: non-small cell carcinoma in the mass and a mediastinal node. PET-CT 10/16: ipsilateral mediastinal nodal disease, no distant disease. Brain MRI 10/18: negative.

Meds: tiotropium, albuterol prn. Allergies: none known.
Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.

Exam: thin, ECOG 1. Decreased breath sounds right upper lung field. No adenopathy. No edema.

Stage: IIIA (cT2a N2 M0).
Discussed at thoracic tumor board 10/21: N2 disease, not a surgical candidate up front.

Plan:
- Definitive concurrent chemoradiation: carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 45 mg/m2 weekly with radiation 60 Gy in 30 fractions, starting 11/04.
- If no progression after chemoradiation, consolidation durvalumab for 12 months.
- Smoking cessation strongly advised; improves outcomes during radiation.
- Radiation oncology simulation this week.

cc: primary care, pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - new lung cancer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in with his sister to go over everything after seeing oncology Tuesday.

S: Stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe with mediastinal nodes, no distant spread on PET or brain MRI. Plan is chemo + radiation together starting 11/4, then an immunotherapy drug for a year. Cough the same, weight holding. Smoking down to a few a day. Mood: 'scared, but I'd rather know.' Sleep ok. No SI.

O: Vitals as charted. Tired-appearing but engaged. Lungs: decreased breath sounds right upper chest, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. NSCLC stage IIIA - oncology/radiation oncology leading. Reviewed the plan with him and his sister, answered questions about side effects. He knows he can text me through treatment.
2. Tobacco: down to a few a day. Offered nicotine patch and varenicline again - wants to finish quitting on his own. Encouraged.
3. COPD: stable, continue tiotropium/albuterol.
4. Mood: understandable stress; PHQ-2 2. Will check in.
5. Flu and updated COVID vaccine today, before chemo starts.
Follow up after chemoradiation.

medications.sig: AUC 2 IV weekly with radiation, 11/04/2024 to 12/13/2024
45 mg/m2 IV weekly with radiation, 11/04/2024 to 12/13/2024

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY - END OF TREATMENT SUMMARY
Treatment dates: 11/04/2024 - 12/13/2024
Diagnosis: non-small cell lung carcinoma, right upper lobe, stage IIIA (cT2a N2 M0).
Treatment: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the right upper lobe primary and involved mediastinal nodes, with concurrent weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 45 mg/m2 given by medical oncology.
Course: completed all 30 fractions and all weekly chemotherapy doses. No treatment breaks.
Follow-up: CT chest about 4 weeks after completion; medical oncology to start consolidation durvalumab if no progression.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Chemoradiation completed 12/13 without breaks. Med list updated with chemo course. Will see him in January.
